36: The intake matrix and failure log are authoritative for actually available fields. Geometry overlap does not establish common visibility; absent support is never a maliciousness label. Preserve raw intensity; do not pool across sensors or import detector-specific clipping as evidence normalization.

17: Choose D as the implementation baseline because it needs the fewest verified quantities and reuses valid counting code. Compare G alone and max(D,G) only for sensor roles whose compensation is validated. If G is unavailable on a frame, its predeclared arm abstains; D-only remains a separately named arm with its own threshold. If D itself has no valid support, return unknown and report feasibility failure. This choice permits a narrow or negative result rather than manufacturing a detector for every attack.

23: Input: finite current XYZ from the same production reader, sensor identity and its frozen coordinate adapter, fixed range/azimuth cells in a validated sensor-relative frame. Context is stream ID × cell ID; range is cell geometry in metres, not sender-claimed pose or current-cloud range extrema. No dynamic region resizing, point-share normalization or context pooling across devices. If sensor origin is not validated, sensor-range D is blocked; a separately documented raw-coordinate count diagnostic remains uncalibrated.

29: Likely sensitivity: sufficiently large additions/density concentration. Evasions: additions below reference tails, removal, rearrangement preserving counts per cell, attacks outside crop and realistic structure. Confounders: traffic density, view/range changes, surfaces/reflectivity, sampling variation, rain/noise, crop crossings. D=0 means no excess detected; it says nothing about absence, honesty or completeness. Present empty is raw zero and can give no surplus where references exist; absence/malformed input is unknown. Reference data, not current sender content, determines normalization. Runtime O(N+cells) with indexed counts, memory one cloud plus small counts; old O(N×400) loops are illustrative, not a real runtime guarantee.

37: Normalize this scalar using the same upper-tail q95/scale rule, fitted per sensor × elapsed-gap bin ([0,.15], (.15,.3], (.3,.5] seconds initially); fallback sensor-only across supported gaps if clean fit permits, otherwise unknown. Gap bins are experimental assumptions to confirm against recording cadence, not measured delay. Minimum 200 clean pairs across >=2 training segments; zero-scale handling as for D. Reference fit uses actual causal pairs from clean training replay; calibration passes new clean pairs through the identical pipeline.

41: Use a spatial index (CPU nearest-neighbor or bounded voxel-neighborhood search with documented approximation); avoid N×N matrices. Target one previous voxel cloud per sensor, <=4 GiB RSS, <=1 s/event initially. Measure actual runtime and cap the development diagnostic at 50,000 deterministic spatially selected centroids per cloud, reporting downsampling and approximation. If budget is exceeded, mark blocked/limited and amend before comparison rather than silently change resolution per scene.

51: Separate instantaneous records from [temporal state](temporal_spec.md). No onset schedule, labels or masks enter either. Retain all factor failures, partial support, invalid readings and no-power outcomes; they are technical dispositions, not evidence of maliciousness.

Never invent its contents. Do not import the old repository wholesale, install its old environment by default, resume its stages, or relabel old count scores as feature reliability.

59: These are seed references, not an exhaustive or already-completed review. If a PDF fails to load, find a legitimate author/venue copy and mark access status. 72: Produce a closest-prior-work table for our candidate contribution. Attribute borrowed mathematics precisely. If the proposed support/traversal idea is substantially covered by existing work, say so. A meaningful result might instead be efficient implementation, calibrated selective reliability, a different information boundary, rigorous evaluation, or an informative failure study. Do not invent novelty by renaming a ratio.

78: Build an evidence-backed decision table: annotation availability/completeness and license; agent counts and principal independence; temporal continuity; sensor origin/calibration and ray semantics; synchronization; heterogeneous sensors; feature-framework compatibility; usable pretrained encoder/fusion checkpoints; train/test provenance; installation risk; compute/storage/download cost; and alignment with our threat model. Do not abandon useful local data merely because it contains raw points, or retain it merely because we already downloaded it.

92: For every candidate define its estimand, all variables/units, inputs available at decision time, proposal/association mechanism, score equation, fitting/calibration, unknown conditions, causal state updates, theoretical properties that can actually be shown, failure cases, and full runtime/memory/communication complexity. Explain why its evidence should track the chosen target, not merely why the formula is bounded. Give falsifying cases and conditions in which two different worlds produce identical allowed inputs.

97: - A ray terminating before an object can indicate occlusion. A ray passing through a proposal envelope and returning farther away is not automatically proof the object is false: boxes contain empty space, rays can pass around non-solid shape parts, materials/multiple returns matter, and timing/pose error can misalign a moving object. State the occupancy/surface model that licenses a contradiction and test violations.

105: Consider whether temporal consistency, independently supported occupancy, cross-view residuals, robust aggregation, or a small calibrated classifier adds complementary evidence. Prevent double counting correlated signals. Freeze learning/reference updates appropriately and test history poisoning, on/off attacks, long silence, reset, recovery and stale evidence. Show both instantaneous estimates and temporal state; do not smooth away critical short failures or reset at evaluator-known attack offsets.

107: Finish with a reasoned shortlist, recommended minimal method, alternative if its feasibility fails, and explicit unresolved assumptions. Select based on literature and clean development feasibility, not on desired held-out attack curves.

120: Do not call direct tensor edits physically realizable laser attacks. Report intended injection, successful serialization/reload, actual feature/raw change and resulting task harm separately. Zero-effect and failed attacks remain visible.

130: Define all denominators, eligibility, empty classes, abstention, preexisting alarms, censoring and failed-injection handling in advance.
